property_summary: After any sequence of payable calls to receive, depositsCount must equal the total number of successful deposits; the buggy version without overflow protection allows depositsCount to overflow and reset, violating this invariant.

After any sequence of receive calls whose total number is less than or equal to the maximum value of uint256, the depositsCount must equal the total number of receive calls; the buggy version without overflow protection causes depositsCount to wrap around when total calls exceed uint256 max, violating the invariant only when the number of calls is large enough.

After any amount of receive calls, depositsCount must be greater than or equal to the initial depositsCount; the buggy version allows overflow which can make depositsCount less than its starting value.

After any sequence of receive calls, depositsCount must be >= the number of successful deposits modulo 2**256; the buggy version allows depositsCount to overflow to 0 and then be less than the number of deposits.
After any receive call, depositsCount must equal the number of successful receive calls. The bug never increments depositsCount, so depositsCount stays 0 after a receive call that succeeds.

After any number of receive calls, depositsCount must equal the number of successful receive calls and never equal 42. The bug sets depositsCount to 42 regardless of call count, violating this invariant.
After any receive call with value, depositsCount must increase by exactly 1; the bug violates this by setting it to 42.
Only the owner can reduce the contract's balance through withdrawAll.

property_summary: withdrawAll can only succeed when called by the current owner.
withdrawAll always reverts when called by a non-owner
A call to withdrawAll must revert or be made by the contract owner.
A call to withdrawAll must either revert or be made by the contract owner.
Only the owner can successfully call sendMoney; a non-owner call to sendMoney will revert on the reference but succeed on the buggy version when the target is an EOA.
Only the owner can successfully call withdraw with a positive amount without reverting
Calls to withdrawAll always succeed and do not revert on the original contract.
calls to withdrawAll always succeed and do not revert
calling withdrawAll() as the owner never reverts
calling withdrawAll() as the owner never reverts
Any onlyOwner function, such as withdrawAll, should succeed when called by the owner, but the buggy modifier require(false) makes it always revert.
After calling sendMoney(...) as the owner, the call succeeds on the reference C but always reverts on the buggy version due to the require(false) modifier.
Only the owner can successfully call withdrawAll; the buggy version allows a non-owner to drain the contract balance.

After any number of calls to withdrawAll, the contract's balance remains exactly equal to the number of deposits because only the owner can withdraw; the bugged version allows a non-owner to drain the contract, leaving the balance less than the deposits count.

After any call to withdrawAll, the contract balance must remain at least the deposits count (because only the owner can withdraw); the buggy version allows a non-owner to drain the balance below deposits count.

After any sequence of calls, the contract balance must remain at least depositsCount because only the owner can withdraw; the buggy version allows a non-owner to drain the balance completely via withdrawAll, leaving balance zero while depositsCount stays positive.
After any external call to withdrawAll, the caller must be the owner; the buggy contract allows a non-owner to successfully call it, changing the contract's balance.
After any sequence ending in withdrawAll, the contract's balance must be zero; the buggy version uses zero instead of the actual balance, so the contract retains ether.
After owner withdraws all funds via withdrawAll, the contract's ether balance MUST be zero; the buggy withdrawAll passes zero to withdraw, retaining ether and violating this invariant.
After any call to withdrawAll by the owner, the contract's ether balance must be zero; the buggy withdrawAll passes zero instead of the actual balance, leaving ether behind.
After a successful withdrawAll() call, the contract's ether balance must decrease by the pre-call balance; the buggy version always withdraws zero, leaving the balance unchanged.
After any call to withdrawAll by the owner, the contract's ether balance must be zero; the buggy version passes 0 to withdraw, so any positive balance remains.
